maya-devsec: Heads-up: RBAC change (RLS enable) is rolling to prod tonight. We need to confirm audit coverage + customer-facing validation for audit events. Also worried about KMS overhead on high-volume tenants — could cause ingest backpressure. Anyone on call?
sam-platform: On it. Which fields are new? Do we need an ES mapping migration or can we do compatibility mapping?
maya-devsec: Quick schema diff we talked about earlier:
```
- event: { actor, action, resource }
+ event: { actor, action, resource, actor_role?, rls_scope?, resource_lease_id?, schema_version }
```
sam-platform: Ok. I think add `schema_version` and make new fields nullable. For customer-facing validation, we should reject malformed events with a clear 400 + error_code so integrators can fix.
liz-sre: FWIW KMS calls per-event will add CPU & latency. If every event triggers an HSM call we'll overload the shipper. We should envelope encrypt: shipper encrypts with per-shard DEK, DEK wrapped by KMS (rotate async). That avoids per-event KMS RPCs.
tom-oncall: Agree on envelope DEK. Also we need backpressure controls at the producer/shipper level: token-bucket per-tenant + batch flush defaults. Recommend: batch_size=512, flush_interval=200ms default, and a burst limit tied to reserved capacity.
sam-platform: For indexing cost, decide field types now: actor_role -> keyword, rls_scope -> keyword, resource_lease_id -> keyword (maybe sparse). Avoid analyzers. Also add `redacted` boolean when PII removed so search UI knows.
audit-bot: schema-change: added fields [actor_role, rls_scope, resource_lease_id, schema_version]; default null for older events.
liz-sre: Index size note: new keyword fields will increase doc size. For high-volume tenants we should: 1) downsample verbose debug events; 2) store raw payload in cold tier (S3) and index minimal fields only; 3) consider nested docs for repeated attrs.
maya-devsec: Customer-facing validation rule: if payload fails schema_version v2 contract -> return 400 with `audit_error: schema_mismatch` and sample rejected payloads to secure S3 for debugging (encrypted). No customer data logged in plain.
tom-oncall: For runtime protection: if shipper queue length > 5000 or *avg_processing_ms* > 2500ms trigger tenant throttling policy and alert to #incidents. We should also add a fallback: mask body and forward minimal envelope to avoid service outage.
sam-platform: I'll implement the validation library and a compatibility flag `accept_legacy=true|false` per tenant so enterprise customers can opt-in to strict validation. Will open PR with tests.
liz-sre: I'll run a cost projection: index growth, expected IOPS, and KMS call reduction with envelope approach. Expect ~30-40% lower KMS calls and ~15% index growth in worst-case.
maya-devsec: Action items: (1) sam-platform — add validation lib + schema_version header + PR (owner: @sam-platform, due: EOW); (2) tom-oncall — shipper token-bucket & batch defaults + alert (owner: @tom-oncall, due: 2 days); (3) liz-sre — cost estimate + mapping proposal + cold-tier plan (owner: @liz-sre, due: EOW); (4) sam+liz — design envelope KMS wrapping plan and migration steps (due: next Wed).
sam-platform: Ack, will attach sample events and migration notes.
tom-oncall: I'll add the shipper health dashboard panels and a runbook for throttling decisions.
maya-devsec: :thumbsup: Good plan. If we see an immediate surge after deploy, fallback policy = mask payload and accept minimal audit envelope until KMS/envelope rollout complete. Keep me posted in thread.
audit-bot: noted action items created: ISSUE-4223, RUNBOOK-shipper-throttle.
